page: Microsoft Azure FX64mds_v2 is a compute-optimized, memory-intensive virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is configured with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores across an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8. It carries 1344.0 GB of system memory, providing 21.0 GB per vCPU, alongside 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs allocated.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput across parallel computational workloads. Multi-threaded processing excels, registering a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 85402.59 and strong stress-ng multi-core performance of 70926.61, supported by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19917.0. Single-core performance sits in the middle range with a stress-ng metric of 2171.29 and Geekbench single-core score of 2095.0. Memory throughput achieves top-tier levels during large uncached reads at 392.4 GB/sec and writes at 170.98 GB/sec. Application testing shows top-tier database operation benchmarks at 37190.82 along with 95.28 million Redis SET operations per second and 97.07 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The qualitative cost profile is characterized by massive resource consolidation. The extreme 21:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio paired with high-frequency CPU cores provides a platform for workloads that require both heavy compute capability and massive in-memory capacities. The primary tradeoff lies in the lack of dedicated GPU hardware, which caps very large-scale artificial intelligence execution despite strong small and medium CPU-based LLM inference metrics. This configuration matches large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), heavy compilation tasks, data science pipelines, and intensive caching layers.
